text:
Anya Ramos: Quick question — legal flagged the SOC2 docs wording around retention. Current line says 'retain audit logs for 7 years' which feels too absolute. Can we add an 'evidence retention' section with clear examples for Hosted vs Private plus a tiny SDK export snippet? PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/docs/pull/1409

Tom Nguyen: +1. We should differentiate 'operational logs' (shorter) vs 'exported evidence' (longer). Proposed draft: 'Redwood retains operational audit logs for a default period; customers can export and retain audit evidence for compliance purposes. Hosted defaults: 90 days operational; exportable evidence retention up to 7 years. Private: customer-managed retention and KMS.' Thoughts?

Maria Patel: That phrasing is better. Legal will care about the baseline minimum. My suggested examples for the section:
• Hosted (default): operational logs retained for 90 days; export API allows you to pull and store evidence for up to 7 years.
• Dedicated/Dedicated+Private: retention is configurable by customer (we recommend 3 years minimum for SOC2 evidence).
I'll draft the snippet showing the export API and a retention_metadata field.

Legal Bot: FYI — SOC2 evidence expectations vary by control area, but 3 years is a reasonable baseline. For certain regulated sectors (finance/healthcare) recommend 6–7 years. Please ensure we phrase as guidance and not a guarantee for all customers.

Chris Lee: I pushed a small PR with the proposed text and a Python SDK example calling the export endpoint: https://github.com/redwood/inference/docs/pull/1409/files
Snippet in PR:
```python
# export audit evidence
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'])
resp = client.audit.export(
  start_time="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  end_time="2025-12-31T23:59:59Z",
  retention_policy={"retain_until":"2032-01-01T00:00:00Z","reason":"regulatory"}
)
print(resp.url)
```

Maria Patel: Couple of nits: 1) Use 'evidence export' consistently (not 'export API' in one place and 'export' in another). 2) Show a JSON example of retention metadata we store (so customers know what to store with their evidence). Example: `{"retain_until":"2032-01-01T00:00:00Z","control_area":"logging","exported_by":"customer-123"}`

Tom Nguyen: Also note: for Hosted we should not promise specific key management details beyond 'encrypted at rest'. Reserve details like KMS/HSM for Private deployments: "Hosted: data encrypted at rest and in transit; key management handled by Redwood. Private: supports customer KMS or HSM integrations."

Anya Ramos: Good catch. I'll update the PR to: 1) Add an 'evidence retention' subsection with the Hosted vs Private examples, 2) include the Python SDK snippet and a JSON retention_metadata example, 3) add the legal guidance sentence from @Legal Bot.

Docs Bot: Pull request opened: #1409 — Anya Ramos updated docs/evidence-retention.md (please review) :github:

Chris Lee: Thanks. Action items: Anya to update the PR; Legal to confirm final retention language (3 vs 7 yrs) and approve phrasing; Docs/Eng to sanity-check SDK snippet and the sample JSON. I'll do a quick pass on formatting after Legal signs off.

Maria Patel: One more small item — add a redaction example for PII in audit events. Something like:
```json
{
  "event": "user.login",
  "user": "REDACTED",
  "ip": "REDACTED",
  "meta": {"reason":"redacted_for_privacy"}
}
```
That helps auditors see how we recommend storing evidence while protecting PII.

Anya Ramos: Perfect. I'll add the redaction snippet and ping everyone when updated. Thanks! :thumbsup:
